story.text: An agent that wants to be findable on-chain may anchor its outcome in a public agent registry (an ERC-8004-shaped lane, opt-in). Three rules keep the anchor honest. First: the anchor is EVIDENCE, never authority — the verdict is made at the gate, by the assessment and [[The Two Gates]]; the chain entry only makes the outcome discoverable.

Second: digests and tier only. No probe content, no scores, no rationales ever leave the gate — minimised disclosure survives anchoring. Third: [[Revocation]] mirrors. A revoked credential posts its revocation mark to the same registry, so on-chain and off-chain relying parties fail the agent together.

The anchor also completes [[The Pool]]'s admission predicate: membership may require a valid credential AND a live anchored entry — a public, chain-native membership rail outside, minimised disclosure inside. The composition happens pool-side; the engine never learns chains exist.
